per_depth.common_affordance: The pairwise-different constraint over exactly two roster values is precisely an undirected graph bipartite-coloring constraint.

The exact-sum-3 rule over the two allowed values 1 and 2 is exactly the condition that every logged edge joins opposite binary colors, reducing the entire task to bipartite graph checking and coloring.
The exact-sum-3 condition on binary states is exactly an undirected graph bipartiteness/2-colorability constraint.
The exact-sum-3 condition on two binary levels is equivalent to requiring opposite colors on every bond, reducing the entire task to bipartite graph testing plus component orientation.
The bond restrictions are exactly a bipartite two-coloring constraint.

Because each endpoint level is 1 or 2, every bond contributes at most 1 to the energy, and requiring the sum of m contributions to equal m forces every bond to contribute 1; the task is therefore exactly bipartite graph coloring plus lexicographic orientation.

per_depth.shortcut_name: reducing the score constraint to graph bipartiteness
per_depth.common_affordance: The bond score is 5 exactly when its two endpoint levels differ, while it is 4 when they are equal; therefore total score 5m is exactly the graph bipartiteness constraint.
The two available intervals intersect at exactly one point if and only if they are different, making every bond an XOR/opposite-color constraint and reducing the whole problem to bipartite checking.

The chosen coefficients and target make the energy decompose per edge: a (1,2) or (2,1) edge contributes 2, while (1,1) contributes -2 and (2,2) contributes -8, so E = 2m if and only if every edge joins unlike states.
